pages.text: "Jam!" Little brother Mumu's eyes sparkled at the jar on the kitchen table. Mom from the mill spread one spoonful on bread. "Just one spoonful." "The biggest bread at dinner is mine!" Mumu munched.
While Mom was in the yard, Mumu plunged a spoon into the jar. "Just one more spoonful, one more..." The spoon scraped the bottom. Soon all the jam was gone.

Dinner came, with a big steaming loaf on the table. Big sister Dodo was already eating. Mumu slumped in his chair, both wings on his belly. "Ooh, I can't fit even one bite..." Beside the jam jar, only his plate was empty.
Mom rubbed his tummy. "Jam filled you up. No room for bread." A drop appeared at Mumu's eye corner. "But I want bread..." Mom held his wing. "I'll teach you how to eat just a little."
Mom whispered, "Your tummy is a little wheat sack. Fill it with jam, and there's no room for bread." Mumu imagined bread stamping its feet outside a jam-filled sack. "Oh! I need to leave space!"
"Leave this much room for bread." Mom spread her wingtips just a little. "One spoonful of jam—meals first!" Dodo spread her wingtips the same amount. "I'll keep it too!"
At snack time the next day, Mom spread one spoonful of jam on bread. Mumu ate only that and set the spoon down firmly. He didn't open the jar! "One spoonful of jam—meals first!"
At dinner, Mumu's tummy rumbled. Holding the biggest loaf in both wings, he ate happily. "Wow! Bread was this tasty?" Dodo ate beside him. Mumu flicked his tail once.
Now Mumu did it easily. "One, one spoonful of jam! Two, meals first! Three, the jar opens only when Mom opens it!" Next time too, just one spoonful, then stop! One spoonful of jam—meals first!
Mom hugged Mumu. "Our wonderful duck knows how to wait too!" Just a little jam makes meals taste better. Mumu called, "One spoonful of jam—meals first!"
